title: Dear Taurus…
old_caption: Dear Taurus: a patchwork blanket, popcorn, and a 'new plans?' text met with the blanket pulled higher. We get it. Tag the Taurus who needs to say yes to one new thing.

title: Your ex just texted
old_caption: "Hey stranger" from an ex can stir everything up. Feeling the pull is normal. Leaving it unanswered is allowed. You're looking for someone new, not someone again.

title: Dear Virgo…
old_caption:
Virgo, your standards come from care, but a checklist that never ends can crowd out a real person.
Someone isn't a project to perfect. Let them be a little messy, and see where date two goes.

title: The Auntie Council
old_caption:
The aunties came with a whole list, but the part that matters is simpler: a little push is normal, and laughing at the same things counts for a lot.
Nobody is perfect for you. Look for who is worth the work.

title: The Star Talk Awards.
old_caption: This award goes to you, for showing up even when it was awkward and staying kind through all of it. The best love stories aren't the flashiest ones. They're the gentle ones.

title: Baggage Claim.
old_caption: Trust issues, an ex's hoodie, feelings that won't fit in a carry-on. Everyone arrives with something. The right person doesn't flinch. They grab a handle and help you carry it.

title: The Aunties Heard
old_caption: Right after a breakup, the urge to send the long message is real. You don't have to. You don't need closure from them to heal. You can give it to yourself, soup and all.

title: Saturday Morning Stars.
old_caption: Coffee made, last slice saved, the appointment remembered. Little acts of care are easy to miss. Notice who does them for you, and tell them thank you. It means more than you'd think.

title: The Comet.
old_caption:
Jealousy can turn "it's fine" into a passive-aggressive draft fast. Your star chose another way: "that made me a bit jealous. can we talk?"
Say it kindly, before it starts to orbit.

title: Love Kitchen.
old_caption:
A pinch of sorry and a whole sack of but rarely turns out well. Chef Taurus has the real recipe: own it, skip the but, ask how to fix it.
A real apology has no but.
